blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The Zephyr protocol team, which issues the native assets and ships the mandatory consensus implementation, exercised a holder-facing global transfer control in 2025. HF8 at block 481500 (2025-03-31) disabled ordinary transfers and conversions, allowing only mandatory per-holder audit migrations; HF9 at 508000 paused all transactions; HF10 at 511000 reopened only audit migrations. HF11 at 536000 restored ordinary transfers of the new assets and permanently invalidated non-migrated ZEPHUSD and ZYIELD balances. Official current documentation still states that unaudited assets cannot be sent or received. The issuer-driven transfer halt and balance invalidation establish a demonstrated mutable holder-facing control under the possible tier, even though activation required network adoption of consensus releases. This differs from fusd-freedom-dollar, whose underlying Zano rollback was performed by chain developers rather than the fUSD issuer. Current v2.3.0 commit 67c5f53b878fef41fb5e74c4382d5b7a2f37fd8a retains the historical restrictions behind hardfork-version gates; same-asset ZSD maps to STABLE_TRANSFER and no standing address blacklist, issuer freeze key or privileged holder burn was identified, so true is not established. The official snapshot captured 2026-09-29T07:47:36.883Z at height 874253 reports HF11, 4,512,886.257473004 native ZEPH in reserve and 402,665.6490463683 ZSD circulating. Disclosed collateral is 100% native ZEPH, with 0% independently issuer/custodian-exposed collateral; the direct possible control determines the verdict. No material production wrapper was identified; the discovered EVM bridge remains testnet. Precedent: usdk-orki classifies mutable holder-facing control as possible without a confirmed active blacklist.

oracleRisk.summary: Zephyr's production code fetches pricing records from three hard-coded delivery endpoints but validates every record against one hard-coded RSA public key. Nodes may reuse the last acceptable record for up to ten blocks and derive moving-average and reserve values locally, leaving one signing authority and a bounded last-good-price path.

branchApplicability.rationale: ZSD has one protocol-wide ZEPH reserve and no borrower-specific collateral positions or liquidation branches. The signed pricing record governs system-wide conversions and reserve-ratio gates, so the complete oracle path is represented at top level.
